import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
# Standard Panda URDF joint origins: xyz, rpy; each revolute axis is local +Z
origins=[((0,0,.333),(0,0,0)),((0,0,0),(-np.pi/2,0,0)),((0,-.316,0),(np.pi/2,0,0)),((.0825,0,0),(np.pi/2,0,0)),((-.0825,.384,0),(-np.pi/2,0,0)),((0,0,0),(np.pi/2,0,0)),((.088,0,0),(np.pi/2,0,0)),((0,0,.107),(0,0,0))]
def fk(q,tool=.1034):
 T=np.eye(4)
 for i,(xyz,rpy) in enumerate(origins):
  A=np.eye(4); A[:3,3]=xyz; A[:3,:3]=Rotation.from_euler('xyz',rpy).as_matrix(); T=T@A
  if i<7:
   R=np.eye(4); R[:3,:3]=Rotation.from_rotvec(np.array([0,0,q[i]])).as_matrix(); T=T@R
 B=np.eye(4); B[2,3]=tool
 return T@B
q=np.array([1.717575e-5,-1.047957,.003346,-2.643980,-.004627,1.534943,-2.307513])
print('FK tool',fk(q)[:3,3], 'TCP measured',np.array([.000454,-.171001,1.210063]))
for t in [0,.05,.1,.15,.2]: print(t,fk(q,t)[:3,3])
print('R',fk(q)[:3,:3])
PY
